correctness.rationale: The proof reduces optimal packing-total colorings of complete multipartite graphs to maximum independent sets of their diameter-two total graphs, proves that a largest part supports a maximum total independent set, and characterizes when a prescribed graph edge is unavoidable in all such maximum sets. The only unavoidable case is the edge between the singleton parts of \(K_{n,1,1}\), where a direct exact calculation shows no drop. For every other edge a maximum color-1 set avoiding it yields a one-color drop after deletion. The finite checker independently reconstructs total graphs and exact small packing colorings for all multipartite types through order \(8\) and all \(813\) single-edge deletions.

The forced-edge analysis distinguishing exactly \(K_{n,1,1}\) is therefore additional content.

A later \(S\)-packing-total preprint is retained as a residual risk because only its abstract was accessible.

value.rationale: The initiating paper explicitly proposed packing-total chromatic critical graphs as an unstudied direction. The result gives a natural complete classification on the broad complete-multipartite family, with one explicit infinite exceptional family. It is structural rather than a routine value substitution: the proof identifies exactly when an underlying edge is forced into every maximum total independent set and explains why that obstruction preserves the packing-total chromatic number.
